value: You can work securely with external partners even if they have no Microsoft Entra ID or no in-house technical team.

value: In a hybrid environment, you can configure Microsoft Entra Connect cloud sync to write password changes back.
reason: 'It is configured through' presents cloud sync as the only route; the source says only 'you can configure Microsoft Entra Connect cloud sync to write password change events back'.

value: Administrative units, for example, need it for each administrator scoped to them; members need only the Free licence unless dynamic membership rules are used.
reason: 'Members only need the Free licence' is contradicted by au-licence: 'If you are using rules for dynamic membership groups for administrative units, each administrative unit member requires a Microsoft Entra ID P1 license.'

value: A help desk lead must add and remove members of assigned groups. Which of these roles lets them do that?
reason: 'And nothing more' implies an exact fit, but Groups Administrator can do far more than manage membership; the source only says 'You'll need the Groups Administrator or User Administrator role to add members and owners.'

value: A reverses the rule. C is not how the block works: it stops invitations to that domain. D is wrong: the block applies to sending invitations, which is exactly what is being attempted.

value: A would not explain why only synced users fail. C would affect cloud-only users as well, not only synced ones. D is about inviting guests.
reason: The old text said too few methods gives an error 'not a contact your administrator', but sspr-too-few (same page) says such users 'need to request that an administrator reset their password'.

value: They are now retired: as of May 2026 you must assign Azure role-based access control roles to manage access instead.
reason: The card never says the roles are retired. The retirement note included on the cited page: 'As of May 2026, classic administrator roles are fully retired and you must assign roles in Azure role-based access control (RBAC) to manage access.'

value: From December 2025, Azure automatically gave public-cloud users who still held those classic roles the Owner role at subscription scope.
reason: The old explanation (sign-up account roles) did not say why Owner matters now. Retirement note on the cited page: 'Starting in December 2025, Azure automatically assigned the Owner role at subscription scope to users in the public cloud who were still assigned the Co-Administrator or Service Administrator role.'
